question.problem:
The standard matrix $T$ of a linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{3}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{3}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -6 & 8 & -7 \\ 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, we find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b],$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 & -10 \\ -6 & 8 & -7 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 & -10 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & -27 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 & -10 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & -27 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 28\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get the false statement $0=28.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that  $b\notin \text{Im}(T).$
